payload.title: Honeymoon Planning Service and How It Works
payload.excerpt: A honeymoon planning service is one person who plans and books your honeymoon for you: the flights, the stays, the days in between, all held in a single itinerary. The good ones agree their fee and confirm what is included in writing before you commit to anything.
key_takeaways: A honeymoon planning service plans and books the whole trip for you, so you deal with one person instead of every airline, stay and supplier.
Your Australian consumer rights stay the same whether you book directly or through a planner.
Planning the honeymoon alongside a destination wedding keeps the contacts, the deadlines and the currencies in one plan instead of two.
Decide your dates, length, style and must-haves first, then ask any planner about fees, inclusions, terms, insurance, exchange rates and commissions.

faq.q: What does a honeymoon planning service do?
faq.a: It plans and books the honeymoon on your behalf: flights, stays, experiences and the connections between them, held in one itinerary. You deal with one person rather than every provider.

faq.q: How far ahead should we plan a honeymoon?
faq.a: Work back from your dates rather than a rule. Ask yourselves how fixed your leave is, whether you are travelling in a popular season and whether the honeymoon follows straight on from a destination wedding. The more of those that apply, the earlier it pays to start. Our guide on when to go on honeymoon helps with the timing.

faq.q: How much does a honeymoon planner cost?
faq.a: There is no single price, because planners charge in different ways. Ask each one what the fee is, what it covers and whether they also receive commissions from suppliers, and get the answers in writing. Comparing what each fee includes tells you more than comparing the numbers alone.

faq.q: Whose name should go on our tickets if we travel straight after the wedding?
faq.a: Book travel in the name that is in your passport. If you change your family name because of marriage, you can get a new passport or keep using your current one.
